questions: Is the original between-sample A accuracy change caused by learning context B or by using two different public A validation samples?
Do all A predictions and all A local-cell parameters remain exact across public B-only feedback?
Does no-B feedback ablation reproduce original between-sample accuracy gap?
Does authentic public B feedback alter B predictions and improve B evaluation, proving the B intervention was applied?
frozen_negative: The original unchanged gates(xs) FAIL on seed31 because before-on-VAL_A minus after-on-RETAINED_A exceeds 0.05; preserve that failure exactly regardless of audit.
method: Run original model/source on historical public developer cohorts only. Compare predictions on SAME public samples before and after B feedback; compare original differently sampled VAL_A versus RETAINED_A; no B-feedback ablation. Enumerate all 16 possible legal A input patterns. Verify B receives exactly 320 valid public feedback updates and checkpoint cold restore. Record CPU time and measured peak Python memory. Never edit original source or original test.
decision_rule: If all paired A samples/16 input patterns and A-cell checkpoint payload are byte-identical across B feedback and a no-B ablation matches after-B A scores, classify the original A accuracy difference as sample-composition confounding rather than demonstrated interference/forgetting. Still retain original gate FAIL, and do not claim novel native retention gain.
